name: Planting the Heart
summary: At Lake Al'Ameth, you help Denalan tend a wooden heart taken from a corrupted timberling. After clearing away its moss, he asks you to place it in his planter and see whether it can be healed.

sections.title: A Second Chance at Life
sections.body: Denalan has scraped the foul moss from the wooden heart taken from Blackmoss the Fetid, a corrupted timberling. Yet an unnatural taint still pulses within the wood. Trusting his years of botany and soil tending, the herbalist asks you to bury the heart directly in his personal planter. He hopes the rich nutrients he blended can draw its remaining natural vitality back toward health.

sections.title: The Miracle of Enriched Earth
sections.body: The heart burrows into the soil as soon as it touches the earth, as if moved by primal instinct. Moments later, it rises cleansed of corruption, warm with a gentle, companionable glow. The heart of a fallen, tainted creature has been purified. Its change shows that careful nurturing and sacred earth can restore harmony, even when unnatural blights strike Teldrassil's wild denizens.

faq.q: Where does this tainted heart come from?
aliases: where did the heart come from
faq.answer: The heart came from Blackmoss the Fetid, a corrupted timberling along Lake Al'Ameth's shores. It was choked with foul moss when recovered, before Denalan scraped it clean.

Denalan is a night elf botanist and herbalist with an isolated camp on Lake Al'Ameth's eastern edge. He spends his days studying Teldrassil's plant life, investigating the strange corruption spreading through its boughs, and mixing enriched soils.

faq.q: Why put the heart in a planter instead of destroying it?
faq.answer: Denalan believes nature should be understood and healed rather than simply destroyed. He hopes his nutritive soil can purge the taint and restore the heart's original vitality.

faq.q: What happens when you bury the heart?
faq.answer: On touching the soil, the heart burrows into it. Seconds later, it wriggles back to the surface cleansed of its taint, pulsing gently as an animated companion.

faq.q: Does this cure the corruption of the timberlings?
faq.answer: Only this single salvaged heart is cured. The change shows that individual botanical spirits can be cleansed with care and rich soil, while corruption still spreads across Teldrassil.

faq.q: Why is the soil in Denalan's planter special?
faq.answer: Denalan has spent considerable time experimenting with compost and nutritive soil blends around Lake Al'Ameth. He designed the soil to revitalize sickly flora and purge creeping decay.

angles.text: As a druid, you see a corrupted timberling's core cleansed through rich earth. It is a reassuring sign that natural care can turn back the unnatural taint afflicting the World Tree's boughs.
Denalan's command of nutrient-rich soil and botanical renewal shows how studying the earth can help mend damaged plant life.

As a night elf, you see the kaldorei commitment to stewarding nature in the restoration of living wood and the coaxing of life from fallen forest spirits, even as Teldrassil suffers troubling ailments.
